function.mechanism: Displaces oxygen/air and provides an inert atmosphere; helium is chemically inert and has low solubility, limiting residual levels in food.
common_food_categories: Processing contexts where inert gas is used to limit oxidation or microbial growth

adi.basis: No numerical ADI was established in EFSA's 2024 re-evaluation; the panel concluded no safety concern based on low toxicological concern/inertness and low expected dietary exposure.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded that use of argon (E938) and helium (E939) as food additives does not raise a safety concern, while noting data gaps on use levels and manufacturing impurity characterization.

fda.notes: Affirmed as GRAS direct human food ingredient when used as a processing aid at levels not exceeding current good manufacturing practice; purity must be suitable for intended use.

adi.basis: WHO JECFA database entry for HELIUM (INS 939) lists no numeric ADI; record links to 53rd meeting (1999) report/specification materials.

concerns.summary: High-concentration inhalation of inert gases can displace oxygen and cause asphyxiation, but this is primarily an occupational/accidental inhalation hazard rather than a dietary additive hazard.
EFSA identified uncertainty about potential manufacturing impurities and real-world use-level data due limited submissions during re-evaluation.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2024 concluded no safety concern for E939 food-additive use.
Helium is chemically inert (noble gas) with low toxicological concern in food-use context.
US FDA lists helium as GRAS under 21 CFR 184.1355 with GMP conditions.

adi_exceedance.notes: A numeric ADI is not established; EFSA did not estimate quantitative dietary exposure due insufficient use-level data, but considered expected dietary exposure low when used as an inert packaging gas.

risk_assessment.rationale: Current regulatory evidence indicates very low dietary risk: inert chemistry, low expected food carryover, EFSA no-safety-concern conclusion (2024), and FDA GRAS status. Remaining uncertainty is driven by limited exposure/manufacturing data rather than demonstrated toxicity.
key_factors: No numeric ADI set and no clear dietary toxicity signal
FDA GRAS affirmation with GMP conditions
JECFA record exists without numeric ADI
Residual uncertainty on impurities and actual use-level data
